name: BranchName
statusNote: BranchName is a single CSS rule over an anchor and has not changed in substance for years; alpha is Primer's label.
summary: A git branch name set in monospace on a pale accent chip, linking to the branch by default. Choose it wherever a branch is named in running UI; it is not a Label or Token and has no remove or select behaviour.

inputs.name: href
inputs.description: Where the chip links. Without a link, render it as plain text (the as: span form), which turns the text muted.

anatomy.name: Chip
anatomy.description: An inline box with 2px vertical and 6px horizontal padding, --bgColor-accent-muted fill and --borderRadius-medium corners; no border.

anatomy.name: Text
anatomy.description: The branch name in --fontStack-monospace at the small body size, never underlined.

variants.description: Rendered as an anchor: text in --fgColor-link.
Rendered as any other element: text in --fgColor-muted on the same accent chip.

layout.text: The chip is inline-block: 2px top and bottom and 6px side padding around the text, on the surrounding text's baseline; its height is the inherited line height plus 4px.
The font is --fontStack-monospace at --text-body-size-small; the line height is inherited from the surrounding text, not set.

states.text: --fgColor-link text on --bgColor-accent-muted, no underline; a non-link chip uses --fgColor-muted text.
No change: the module defines no hover style and suppresses the underline.
The module draws no focus style; on the web a linked chip shows the browser's default focus ring on keyboard focus. A native build must draw one.

behaviour.text: A linked chip navigates to href on pointer release or Enter; a text chip does nothing.

keyboard: Tab focuses a linked chip; Enter follows it.
semantics: Its name is the branch name; nothing else is announced.

notes.text: The text colour depends on the element, not a prop: an anchor is --fgColor-link, anything else --fgColor-muted. A native API should expose this as whether href is set.

There is no truncation or maximum width: a long branch name widens the chip, and the browser wraps it only where the name offers a break (after a hyphen), which splits the chip's fill across lines. A native build must choose: no wrap, wrap with a fragmented chip, or truncate with an ellipsis and expose the full name.

minTargetPx is null because the chip sets no height; it is the inherited line height plus 4px (22px when that resolves to 18px, as BaseStyles' unitless 1.5 does at the chip's 12px), and Primer sets no minimum target.
The monospace face is the platform's first available from a CSS font stack (ui-monospace, SF Mono, Menlo, Consolas...); a native build resolves --fontStack-monospace to a concrete font itself.
